To evaluate the quality of the response, we adopt BLEU  and ROUGE  to evaluate the generated response against the reference. Higher scores indicate that the generated results are closer to the reference. We also evaluate the diversity of generated response by n-grams distinct . Following previous works in evaluating faithfulness , we take the NLI, Q 2 F1 and Q 2 NLI  as metrics.

In addition to reference-based metrics, comprehensive human evaluation is crucial for dialogue-related generation tasks. To this end, we randomly selected 100 samples with two responses (from sequence- or graph-based models) from each dataset for each architecture, and instructed annotators to choose the preferred response based on dialogue history and given knowledge.
